title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Customer Churn Prediction in Telecommunications: A Framework for CRM Integration
summary: Telecom churn models can rank at-risk subscribers, but opaque ensembles are hard to translate into retention actions, so the paper studies explainable churn prediction and CRM integration. It benchmarks Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM on the IBM Telco Customer Churn benchmark (7,043 records, 19 features, SMOTE on the training partition only), then applies SHAP/LIME and designs a four-layer CRM workflow. Logistic Regression obtains the best test AUC-ROC (0.8411), LightGBM the best accuracy (78.42%), all four sit within a 0.011 AUC band, and the framework projects $199K–$319K preserved per campaign cycle for the top-risk quintile.

claims.est_compute: CPU, ~1–3 min for LR after preprocessing; full pipeline <10 min
claims.quote: Logistic Regression posts the best AUC-ROC (0.8411) and the highest recall (78.34%) after SMOTE balancing

match_target.why: C1 is the paper's headline AUC result and the user's explicit target: a single L2 logistic regression on public tabular data is the cheapest way to demonstrate the central finding, requiring no tree ensembles, SHAP stack, or CRM simulation.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUC-ROC is printed as a fraction in [0,1] and evaluated on n=1,409 (<2,000), so the bounded-score band is 0.02 absolute; no test-set standard deviation is reported for C1.

requirements.stmt: Use the IBM Telco Customer Churn CSV with 7,043 records and 21 columns; drop customerID and Churn to leave 19 predictors, with Churn as the binary target.
requirements.quote: Dropping the customer identifier and the churn label from the benchmark’s 21-column schema leaves 19 predictive features

requirements.stmt: Label-encode gender and the binary yes/no fields Partner, Dependents, PhoneService, and PaperlessBilling to {0,1}; leave SeniorCitizen as already 0/1.
requirements.quote: Gender and binary yes/no features (Partner, Dependents, PhoneService, PaperlessBilling) are label-encoded to {0,1}.

requirements.stmt: One-hot encode MultipleLines, InternetService, OnlineSecurity, OnlineBackup, DeviceProtection, TechSupport, StreamingTV, StreamingMovies, Contract, and PaymentMethod with all levels, yielding 40 features.
Min-max scale the continuous features tenure, MonthlyCharges, and TotalCharges to [0,1].
requirements.quote: Continuous features are min-max scaled to [0,1]. A stratified 80/20 train–test split preserves the class ratio

requirements.stmt: Use a stratified 80/20 train-test split preserving the churn ratio; the held-out test partition must contain 1,409 records.
requirements.quote: A stratified 80/20 train–test split preserves the class ratio across partitions.

requirements.stmt: Apply SMOTE only to the training partition using five nearest neighbours, producing 8,278 balanced training records; never oversample the test set.
requirements.quote: SMOTE is applied exclusively to training data: synthetic minority instances are interpolated between each real churner and one of its five nearest neighbours

requirements.stmt: Train Logistic Regression with L2 regularisation as the primary interpretable model.
requirements.quote: Logistic Regression (l2 regularisation) serves as the interpretable linear baseline against which non-linear methods are measured.

requirements.stmt: Use a fixed 0.5 decision threshold for every classifier and do not tune the threshold post hoc.
requirements.quote: All models use a 0.5 decision threshold for class assignment, with no post-hoc threshold tuning, preserving comparability.

requirements.stmt: Configure Random Forest with 400 CART trees, maximum depth 12, minimum leaf size 8, sqrt(p) features per split, and bootstrap sampling.
requirements.quote: Random Forest aggregates 400 CART trees (max depth 12, min leaf 8, √p features per split) via bootstrap sampling.

requirements.stmt: Use the official xgboost and lightgbm libraries for the boosted-tree models, falling back to scikit-learn equivalents only if unavailable.
requirements.quote: XGBoost and LightGBM rows use the official libraries.

requirements.stmt: Compute AUC-ROC from predicted probabilities via trapezoidal integration and evaluate all reported metrics only on the held-out test set.
requirements.quote: Classifier performance on the test set (n = 1,409); best value per metric in bold, AUC-ROC via trapezoidal integration.

requirements.stmt: For the Logistic Regression global explanations, compute SHAP values for every test instance using shap's LinearExplainer and rank features by mean absolute SHAP value.
requirements.quote: We compute Shapley values for every test instance of the primary model (Logistic Regression) with the shap library’s LinearExplainer

requirements.stmt: For local explanations, use lime's LimeTabularExplainer in classification mode, quartile-discretise the three continuous features, and declare binary and one-hot columns categorical.
Implement CRM risk tiers with High for p > 0.70, Medium for 0.40 ≤ p ≤ 0.70, and Low for p < 0.40.
requirements.cite: Section III-E, CRM Integration Design; Section V-B
requirements.quote: High (p > 0.70), Medium (0.40 ≤p ≤0.70), and Low (p < 0.40) risk tiers

requirements.stmt: Monitor PSI on incoming feature distributions and trigger retraining when PSI exceeds 0.20.
requirements.quote: monitoring on incoming feature distributions triggers model retraining when PSI exceeds 0.20.
